title: Token-span compactor and touch-frequency reserver for paged KV cache
creator: Michael Chen
description:
Problem: Paged attention workloads show degraded p95/p99 decode latency during long-context sessions due to scattered token residence across many small pages and frequent short-lived page pinning. This increases GPU memory fragmentation and causes expensive eviction churn when new prefill/decode waves arrive.

Proposal: Implement a two-part runtime feature: 1) a token-span compactor that opportunistically merges adjacent small live spans within a page into contiguous allocation segments to reduce page pressure and improve decode locality; 2) a touch-frequency reserver that predicts near-term re-access probability for spans using a lightweight exponential recency counter and places soft reservations for high-touch spans in a small fast reservoir to avoid premature eviction. The design aims to reduce forced page migrations and lower p99 prefill stalls without changing public APIs or tenant isolation semantics.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end benchmark showing >=10% reduction in p99 prefill latency on long-context chat traces compared to baseline
GPU memory fragmentation score reduced by >=15% on synthetic multi-tenant stress test
No regression in single-request tail latency for short-context workloads (<=1% increase in p99)
Feature behind runtime flag and configurable per-tenant parameters (reservoir size, compaction aggressiveness)
Unit and integration tests covering compaction correctness and reservation expiry semantics
success_metrics: average number of page evictions per 1k requests reduced by >=20%
memory reclamation efficiency increased (live bytes per page) by >=12%
no increase in overall token cost observed in 24h smoke run
implementation_notes: Compactor runs as a background cooperative pass on GPU shard threads during low-util intervals; uses epoch markers to avoid interfering with active decodes
Compaction is limited to spans that are contiguous in logical token order and have no outstanding KV references (soft liveness check)
Reservoir uses a tiny LRU with exponential recency counters (alpha=0.25 default) and a fast admit/evict path optimized for the common-case hit
Expose per-tenant knobs via dedication config: reservoir_size, compaction_threshold_bytes, compaction_budget_ms
Implement slow-path verification in debug builds to assert no pointer aliasing after compaction
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.token_span_compaction and runtime.touch_reserver
Stage 1: internal shadow run on staging with representative production traces for 48h
Stage 2: enable for 5% of production tenants (low-traffic) and monitor memory fragmentation and tail latency for 72h
Stage 3: increase to 25% if metrics stable, then 100% after 2 successful cycles
Rollback: feature toggle off; compaction is idempotent and reservoir drains on toggle disable
test_plan: Microbenchmarks: compile-time tests for compaction correctness and reservoir eviction ordering
Integration: long-context chat replay (10k sessions) to measure evictions, page migrations, and tail latency
Fault injection: simulate decode preemption and mid-compaction aborts to verify safety
A/B canary: compare 0% and 5% tenant cohorts with end-to-end observability dashboards
Perf regression: run full perf-suite (cpu/gpu) on each PR via CI with target thresholds
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: compaction may introduce transient CPU overhead and interfere with hot decode paths -> Mitigation: limit compaction budget and run only on mostly-idle shards
Risk: incorrect compaction could corrupt KV references -> Mitigation: add strict debug assertions and conservative liveness checks before merging spans

Risk: reservoir misprediction could reserve too many pages reducing overall throughput -> Mitigation: expose tuning parameters and implement an adaptive fallback that reduces reservoir admission on throughput drop
Risk: multi-tenant fairness concerns if one tenant monopolizes reservoir -> Mitigation: per-tenant reservoir quotas and cross-tenant admission arbitration
